adds.title: Constitution of Bolivia - Article 14(II)
adds.summary: Bolivia's 2009 Constitution Article 14(II) prohibits and punishes discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, protecting equal recognition, enjoyment and exercise of rights.

adds.title: Constitution of Bolivia - Article 63
adds.summary: Promulgated 7 February 2009, Article 63 of Bolivia's Constitution establishes that marriage is constituted by legal bonds between a woman and a man on equality of rights and duties and that stable, singular free or de facto unions between a woman and a man without legal impediment produce the same personal, patrimonial and parent-child effects as civil marriage, thereby constitutionally limiting recognized marriage and equivalent unions to different-sex couples.

adds.title: Law Against Racism and All Forms of Discrimination (Ley Contra el Racismo y Toda Forma de Discriminacion)
adds.summary: Bolivia's Law No. 045 Against Racism and All Forms of Discrimination, enacted 8 October 2010, defines discrimination to include distinctions based on sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, prohibits such discrimination in employment, services, education, health and other public and private spheres, and criminalizes discriminatory acts with prison terms and fines, thereby establishing legal protection and sanction-based redress applicable to trans persons.

adds.title: Gender Identity Law (Ley de Identidad de Genero)
adds.summary: On 25 November 2015 Bolivia's government presented a Gender Identity Law proposal to allow transsexual and transgender people to change their names and genders on ID cards and birth certificates via civil registry offices, forwarded to the legislative assembly for approval, while explicitly excluding same-sex marriage.
